input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The only governing-law/venue provision (§ 20(h)) selects the laws of Nova Scotia (and Canadian law applicable there) with the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is not among the accepted laws (New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales), so the clause fails the fallback on both material terms (governing law and forum). It is not walk-away territory: the forum is our own home province (Sparkling is in Dartmouth, NS, while Garman is in Saskatoon, SK), the jurisdiction grant is non-exclusive, and there is no arbitration provision anywhere in the agreement. Redline moves the clause to the preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York County courts) while leaving the rest of the sentence structure intact; Delaware, California, or England and Wales/London remains available as a fallback if Garman pushes back.

proposal.summary: Replace Nova Scotia governing law and courts with New York law and exclusive New York County venue.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved governing law and venue to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our standard position; Nova Scotia law is outside our accepted list. We can accept Delaware, California, or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London as an alternative.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
